MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OCTOBER 15, 2018

A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Pope, Persichina, Romanelli, Retz, Wroan, Ciarolla

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  CHAIR ROMANELLI welcomed and congratulated Valerie Ciarolla on her appointment to the Park
  and Activities Commission.

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 17, 2018

  COMMISSIONER POPE had a question regarding Michael Hogue’s concern with the race which
  was scheduled prior to the Hills Are Alive race. Community Services Director Clark stated that it
  did not affect the city’s race.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI inquired about the parade promotions increase and asked if City Council
  had approved the increase. Community Services Director Clark stated that it was approved.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR RETZ to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2018 AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  “BUTCHER PARK” REVISED CONCEPTUAL PLAN DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this was on the last agenda but more time was
  needed to review the revisions. He introduced Baxter Miller with BMLA to provide more
  information on the revisions that were made in order to keep the project within budget.

  Baxter Miller, BMLA provided an overview of the project and stated that the park will still have
  more natural looking features. He stated that most of the change is in the area scope, which was
  pulled in. There will still be swings, climbers, and wood structure design throughout the project.
  The paving elements are sustainable and are all porous. Mr. Miller stated that there may be
  opportunity to pick-up boulders or tree trunks from the county or city in order to use for the project.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER WROAN, Mr. Miller stated that the line item for fill
  was removed but there is still a budget for grading activities due to the need to flatten the surface
  if needed.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN inquired about the change in percent for prevailing wage. Mr. Miller
  stated that it could be due to the product or it may just by a typo, but stated that he will look into
  it further.
   COMMISSIONER WROAN inquired about the bike racks and if there is a bike trail. Mr. Miller
  stated that there is a bike trail.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN inquired about the significant reduction in the budget for irrigation. Mr.
  Miller stated that the park area went from 12,000 sq. ft. to 5,000 sq. ft.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN asked about the boulders. Community Services Director Clark stated
  that the city has stacks of boulders.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ROMANELLI, Mr. Miller stated that yes, the public’s input is
  mostly in the categories of site furnishings and play equipment since they are the most significant
  features of the park. Due to the need to keep the project within budget there were significant
  reductions in features within these categories, but also kept the spirit of the features that the public
  would like to see in the park. CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that his concern is that other elements
  could have been revised in order to keep more features requested by the public.

  Ryan McCormick, Dapplegray Neighborhood, expressed his concern with the removal of the
  safety fence and stated that this is a high traffic area and a fence is important. Mr. McCormick
  suggested researching more cost effective slides to add to the park.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ inquired about the existing vinyl fence and the boulders that were suggested
  to be used as barriers. Mr. Miller stated that there are no plans at this time to remove the existing
  fence, but installing a barrier fence is expensive. Also, regarding the boulders, there is still interest
  in using the boulders, however, moving the boulders to the site can also be costly.

  Community Services Director Clark asked about the cost savings if there was an opportunity for
  the city to get free soil for the site. Mr. Miller stated that there could be a cost savings of
  approximately $2.00/sq. ft., but the most significant cost in moving soil is the equipment and
  personnel, but if it is close by, it can be used to make the park more interesting.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the boulders being used as barriers and asked if they will
  go around the park or in the park. Mr. Miller stated that the boulders will be used as barriers and
  will be placed in the park to discourage using the park as a cut-through.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about seeking the Eagle Scouts to build seating. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that there are some elements that staff may be able to help with in
  order to help with the cost and recommended tabling this item to the next meeting in order to
  prepare a presentation with revisions to show what city staff can help with.

  Mr. Miller stated that there are several revisions that could still be made to answer questions that
  have come up in this meeting.

  Mr. McCormick asked about the circular swing. Mr. Miller stated that he will look into that.

  Sally Kensey, Pony Lane, stated that her and her grandchildren went to Ken Malloy Harbor Park
  and stated that it is done in natives and is a beautiful park. Ms. Kensey suggested planting Yankee
  Point plants to serve as barriers. She also stated that Ken Malloy Harbor Park has metal and
  plastic play equipment that could be found in natural colors and may be more cost effective.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that he will take photographs of the play equipment at
  Ken Malloy Park.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  TABLE THIS ITEM UNTIL THE COMMISSION RECEIVES FURTHER DIRECTION
  FROM STAFF.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the Little Library at Rockbluff Park lost a door, but it is already
  being taken care of.

B.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY CONSULTANT INTERVIEWS UPDATE

  VICE CHAIR RETZ stated that four architectural firms were interviewed and there was one firm
  that stood out. They had a good presentation and provided an example of a project they had

Park & Activities Commission Minutes  2
October 15, 2018
   done. In addition the amount of work for the budget and also they stated that they would dedicate
  a full day to meet with the public at the site. Community Services Director Clark stated that the
  Commission will receive a full packet and references still need to be checked.

C.  PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING – OCTOBER 22, 2018 AT 6:00 P.M.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the meeting will be held on Monday, October 22nd.
  Commissioner Persichina and Portugal will be in attendance and he also invited.
  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to be part of the committee. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  accepted the invitation.

D.  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING MEETING – OCTOBER 30, 2018 AT 6:00 P.M.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this will be a meeting with the City Council. CHAIR
  ROMANELLI asked about the public response with holding the events at separate locations.
  Community Services Director stated that he estimated about 800 attendees and there was no
  issues with parking. The monies for various events was significantly higher than last year. Betty’s
  Foundation event was also well attended and they will pick a date different than the City
  Celebration next year. VICE CHAIR RETZ stated that Betty’ Foundation event was well attended.
  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that both events did well and the equestrian community was
  thrilled to be back at the Empty Saddle Club, there are opportunities for improvement, but it was
  a good event. Betty’s Foundation was excellent and hope that they will continue to use the park
  for their event.

9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEM

A.  PREPARED PENINSULA EXPO – OCTOBER 28, 2018 AT NOON

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this event will be held at the Norris Theatre on
  Indian Peak Road.

B.  NOVEMBER 19, 2018 PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING QUORUM

  The Commissioner’s present stated that they are available for the November 19th meeting.

10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2018

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 9, 2018

C.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 10, 2018

D.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 1, 2018

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2018

11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY CONSULTANT SELECTION

B.  COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO RE-DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the tree in the patio is being removed since the
  roots are growing under the Council Chamber and damaging the plumbing. At the next meeting
  there will be discussion on what can be put in the patio area.

  COMMISSIONER WROAN stated that he would like an item to be added to the next agenda. He
  would like to discuss the west entrance to the Palos Verdes Peninsula to discuss the landscaping
  at the memorial flags site in Palos Verdes Estates.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 7:55 p.m. to the joint meeting of the City Council
  and Park & Activities Commission for the City Celebration Debriefing on Tuesday, October 30,
  2018 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling
  Hills Estates.
